subject: Science
title: Autumn science review and evidence
objective_verbatim: Review and evidence autumn science (Entry Level Science / UAS).
reading_age_est: rough ARI grade 5.83 on 892 pupil-visible words; heuristic age guide 11.83 years, not a formal reading-age test
pupil_words: use a model and a matching clue to show what you know in science.
success_criteria: I can choose a model that fits my question.
I can give a clue that supports my answer.
I can name one next step after feedback.

vocab.definition: a result or observation that supports a claim
vocab.example: A measured distance is evidence about a toy run.

vocab.definition: a push or pull on an object

vocab.example: Earth’s rotation makes day and night.
Climate is not the weather on one day.

retrieval.question: What changed in last week’s fair test?
retrieval.answer: The surface; the toy, start and launch were controls.

retrieval.question: What model can help with a toy motion question?
Name one force you learned in Autumn 1.

stages.pupil_text: Choose a model used this term. Point to one question it could help answer.
stages.adult_text: Offer a predictable seat or standing spot and the first visual cue. No public test.

stages.pupil_text: Think back. Say, point or write one answer for each question.
stages.adult_text: Ask three low-stakes retrieval questions; prior coverage must be checked.

stages.pupil_text: I choose a question, then a matching model and clue. For day and night, the torch lights one side of a turning ball. I explain the place turning into shade. This is practice, not help during formal evidence.
stages.adult_text: Model the full reasoning step, pre-teach four words and ask the show-me question.

stages.pupil_text: In practice, the question and torch-and-ball model are supplied. Complete the missing clue: what happens to the marked place as the ball turns?
stages.adult_text: Show the part-done example, then allow paired talk before an answer. One-minute reset inside this stage.

stages.pupil_text: Show everyone which model best helps explain day and night.
stages.adult_text: All pupils answer the four-option hinge; use the decision rule, not a score.

stages.pupil_text: Choose two science questions from forces, space or climate. Show an answer with a model and a matching clue. Use only your agreed support if this is formal evidence.
stages.adult_text: One adult supports agreed pupils, the other holds the group; swap across the week. One-minute reset inside this stage.

stages.pupil_text: In practice, hear one comment on claim and clue. Self-edit one mismatch. If this is formal evidence, receive and act on feedback after collection under the agreed conditions.
stages.adult_text: Give a specific verbal comment (VF) and invite one self-edit (//) or read-back (?).

stages.pupil_text: Tell the adult what you learned, which clue you used, your feedback and one next step. They use your answer to plan the next model or support.
stages.adult_text: Hear the answer and name how it changes the next example or support. One-minute reset and handoff.

worked_example.full: Question: why does a place get night? → choose torch and turning ball → marked place turns away from light → explain Earth’s rotation.
worked_example.faded: Question: what slowed the toy? → choose toy and surface → observe ____ → explain a possible force; check with repeat runs.
worked_example.removed_step: Identify an observed travel-distance clue for the toy claim, not a space fact.
worked_example.fade_next: Next time remove the supplied model choice in practice and ask the pupil to select it from three familiar kits.

cfu.question: Show me the model you would use for day and night.

hinge.question: A new question asks why a model sled stops sooner on a mat. Which kit can help test it?

options.diagnosis: Uses a rotation model to answer a friction question.

options.text: Two ice cubes on dark card.
options.diagnosis: Uses melting ice rather than a moving sled to test the surface effect.
Uses a single weather report instead of a surface-and-motion test.

hinge.decision_rule: About 3 in 4 or more right → move on. Otherwise re-model with the named I-do example, then ask the parallel hinge.
hinge.parallel_hinge: A new place on a globe turns into shade. Which kit explains that: globe and fixed lamp, or sled and mat? Answer: globe and fixed lamp.

misconceptions.misconception: A melting-ice model tests why a moving sled stops on a surface.
misconceptions.spot: Pupil chooses C, an ice model for sled motion.
misconceptions.correction: Use the sled with two marked surfaces for the process in the question.

misconceptions.misconception: One day’s weather report can explain the sled’s stopping distance.
misconceptions.spot: Pupil chooses D, using one day’s weather to explain the sled.
misconceptions.correction: Observe and compare the sled on surfaces instead of using unrelated weather.

we_do.support: Point to the torch and the marked place before naming the clue.
we_do.stretch: Explain why a correct model can still leave out size, distance or other details.
we_do.F: Point to the torch and the marked place before naming the clue.
we_do.M: Use a model and matching clue to explain a science idea.
we_do.H: Explain why a correct model can still leave out size, distance or other details.

tiers.F: Match one question to its model.
tiers.M: Use a model and matching clue to explain a science idea.
tiers.H: State one limit of a model and suggest a further check.

stems.M: My answer is ___; I saw ___ in the model.
stems.H: The model suggests ___, but I would check ___ because ___.

tiers.go_deeper: For one claim, give two checks and one model limit. Say which extra observation you would seek.
tiers.early_finisher: Compare two model limits. Choose a claim neither can settle alone and name a new observation that would help.

adaptations.cognition_learning: Offer three familiar model cards with one question highlighted, then fade the highlight.
adaptations.communication_interaction: Allow verbal, signed or AAC practice of claim and clue before the independent response.
adaptations.semh: Agree a low-voice check-in and known pause; do not create pressure to perform publicly.
adaptations.sensory_physical: Keep model kit fixed and high contrast; offer TTS and agreed accessible evidence mode.
adaptations.eal: Pre-teach the same four word icons. Keep M/H challenge open with language frames and planning in any language.

ta_focus.independent: Choose your own question. Which clue can you show without my prompt?

prompt_ladder: Point to the lesson’s diagram, kit or source.

F.q: Which model fits day and night?

M.a: It matches the question and claim.

M.q: How can you show a force result?
M.a: Point to or name an observed toy run, with controls noted.

H.q: What is one limit of a torch-and-ball model?
H.a: It is not to scale, among other limits.

H.q: What would strengthen a climate claim?
H.a: Long-term observations, not one weather report.

items: Day and night → torch and ball
interactions.answer_key: The model matches the named question.
For climate, one day’s weather alone cannot establish the long-term pattern.

diagrams.alt: Three separate panels show a toy on two surfaces, sunlight reaching a turning Earth, and one weather day beside a schematic climate line across many years. The climate line is not measured data.
diagrams.caption: Three ideas: toy on two surfaces, day and night, and a long climate pattern. Sketches are simplified; the line is not data.

practical.kind: optional prepared handling rehearsal; not a claimed SoW core practical
practical.kit: Adult-prepared familiar model kit for the selected question
method: Use only the prepared model selected for the agreed practice or formal task.
practical.prediction: Choose the safe feature or answer before moving the prepared model pieces.
practical.results_table: Record the observed feature, source or model answer in the pupil task.
practical.risk: Staff confirm the local school risk assessment and exact prepared kit.
practical.pupil_risk: Loose model parts, a toy launch or a torch beam could cause harm if misused.
practical.pupil_safety: Keep model parts on the tray, launch only with adult permission and aim a torch away from eyes.

facts.claim: Friction is a contact force, and force is a push or pull.
Earth’s turn brings day and night at a place.
Climate is a long-term pattern; one weather report is not itself a climate trend.
A valid science claim should use a matching observation or result and recognise model limits.

stages: Arrival (5 min): Choose a model used this term. Point to one question it could help answer. Staff: Offer a predictable seat or standing spot and the first visual cue. No public test.
Starter (3 min): Think back. Say, point or write one answer for each question. Staff: Ask three low-stakes retrieval questions; prior coverage must be checked.

I Do (5 min): I choose a question, then a matching model and clue. For day and night, the torch lights one side of a turning ball. I explain the place turning into shade. This is practice, not help during formal evidence. Staff: Model the full reasoning step, pre-teach four words and ask the show-me question.

We Do (7 min): In practice, the question and torch-and-ball model are supplied. Complete the missing clue: what happens to the marked place as the ball turns? Staff: Show the part-done example, then allow paired talk before an answer. One-minute reset inside this stage.
We Do 2 (5 min): Show everyone which model best helps explain day and night. Staff: All pupils answer the four-option hinge; use the decision rule, not a score.

Independent (8 min): Choose two science questions from forces, space or climate. Show an answer with a model and a matching clue. Use only your agreed support if this is formal evidence. Staff: One adult supports agreed pupils, the other holds the group; swap across the week. One-minute reset inside this stage.

Review (4 min): In practice, hear one comment on claim and clue. Self-edit one mismatch. If this is formal evidence, receive and act on feedback after collection under the agreed conditions. Staff: Give a specific verbal comment (VF) and invite one self-edit (//) or read-back (?).

Exit (3 min): Tell the adult what you learned, which clue you used, your feedback and one next step. They use your answer to plan the next model or support. Staff: Hear the answer and name how it changes the next example or support. One-minute reset and handoff.

if_behind.must_teach_core: Choose two science questions from forces, space or climate. Show an answer with a model and a matching clue. Use only your agreed support if this is formal evidence. Preserve the individual evidence required above.
if_behind.shorten_or_merge: After a secure hinge, shorten repeated oral rehearsal. If needed, merge the exit reflection into the Arrival of Spring 1 W01. Keep the core evidence and any safety teaching; record the change and coverage impact.
if_behind.next_lesson: Spring 1 W01: Compare and group materials by properties (hardness, conductivity, solubility).
if_behind.dependency: Pass on today’s checked understanding and unresolved hinge errors for the next starter. Do not replace incomplete individual work with a group product.

target_links.Cognition & learning: We do: Identify an observed travel-distance clue for the toy claim, not a space fact. Record the pupil’s own sequencing, attention or independence target, including the prompt level needed.
target_links.Communication & interaction: Check: respond to “A new question asks why a model sled stops sooner on a mat. Which kit can help test it?” in the pupil’s agreed mode. Evidence an individual communication/turn-taking target without requiring speech.
target_links.SEMH: Arrival: Choose a model used this term. Point to one question it could help answer. Use the agreed predictable start or pause/re-entry plan; evidence the pupil’s own regulation or engagement target privately.
target_links.Sensory/physical: Independent: Choose two science questions from forces, space or climate. Show an answer with a model and a matching clue. Use only your agreed support if this is formal evidence. Offer the agreed accessible input, enlarged material or adapted equipment; record the pupil’s target-related access/independence, not a diagnosis.
target_links.EAL: Model/shared rehearsal: use evidence, force, rotation, climate with the actual example; allow first-language planning and oral rehearsal before the independent response. Record the agreed language target; EAL is not SEN.

planning_entry.target_recording: Capture E against the pupil's own IEDP target on the school's evidence app; the IEDP carries their EHCP-linked and Boxall targets, so one record serves every plan. Follow the pupil's IBSP where it differs from these routines.
